questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}$ and $y=3t$.
What is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=2$?

options.why: Divided the wrong way round, using $\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}=\dfrac{4}{3}$ as the gradient.
Used the normal gradient $-\dfrac{3}{4}$ instead of the tangent gradient.
Inverted the quotient and then took the negative reciprocal, giving $-\dfrac{4}{3}$.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{3}+1$ and $y=t^{2}$.
What is the equation of the normal to the curve at the point where $t=2$?

options.why: Gave the tangent, using gradient $\dfrac{1}{3}$ instead of the normal gradient.
Used $-\dfrac{1}{3}$ as the normal gradient, forgetting to invert $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ first.
Used $+3$ as the normal gradient, dropping the negative sign.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{3}-12t$ and $y=t^{2}-2t$.
What are the coordinates of the stationary point on the curve?

options.why: Solved $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$ instead of $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$, which locates a vertical tangent.
Solved $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$ and took the other root, $t=-2$.
Sign error evaluating $x=1-12$ at $t=1$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2t-2$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3t^{2}-12$
$2t-2=0$
$t=1$
At $t=1$, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3-12=-9\neq 0$, so the tangent is horizontal.
$x=1-12=-11$ and $y=1-2=-1$
The stationary point is $(-11,-1)$.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}+2t$ and $y=t^{3}-12t$.
At which point is the tangent to the curve vertical?

options.why: Solved $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$, which gives a horizontal tangent, not a vertical one.
Solved $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$ and took the other root, $t=-2$.
Sign errors substituting $t=-1$ into both equations.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t+2$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3t^{2}-12$
$2t+2=0$
$t=-1$
At $t=-1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3-12=-9\neq 0$, so the tangent is vertical.
$x=1-2=-1$ and $y=-1+12=11$
The tangent is vertical at $(-1,11)$.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}$ and $y=2t^{3}$.
For which value of $t$ does the tangent to the curve have gradient $6$?

options.why: Divided $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=6t^{2}$ by $2$ instead of by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t$.
Multiplied $3$ by $6$ instead of solving $3t=6$.
Divided the wrong way round, solving $\dfrac{1}{3t}=6$.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}$ and $y=8t$.
What is the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point $(4,16)$?

options.why: Took $t=-2$ from $t^{2}=4$ without checking it also satisfies $8t=16$.
Divided the wrong way round, using $\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}=\dfrac{t}{4}$.
Gave the normal instead of the tangent.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=2t$ and $y=t^{2}$.
The normal to the curve at the point where $t=3$ crosses the $y$-axis.
At which point does it cross?

options.why: Used the tangent $y=3x-9$ instead of the normal.
Used $-3$ as the normal gradient instead of $-\dfrac{1}{3}$.
Used $+\dfrac{1}{3}$ as the normal gradient, dropping the negative sign.

questions.solution_text:
At $t=3$: $x=6$ and $y=9$.
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2t=6$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{6}{2}=3$
Normal gradient $=-\dfrac{1}{3}$.
$y-9=-\dfrac{1}{3}(x-6)$
$y=-\dfrac{1}{3}x+11$
Setting $x=0$ gives $y=11$, so the normal crosses at $(0,11)$.

questions.question_text:
A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}-2t$ and $y=t^{3}-3t^{2}$.
The tangent to the curve is horizontal at more than one point.
What are the coordinates of the point where the tangent is horizontal and $t>0$?

options.why: Used the correct parameter $t=2$ but evaluated $x$ as $t^{2}=4$, dropping the $-2t$ term.
Set $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$ to get $t=1$ (that is a vertical tangent, not a horizontal one) and also evaluated $x$ as $t^{2}=1$, dropping the $-2t$ term.
Set $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$ instead of $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$, giving $t=1$; that is where the tangent is vertical, not horizontal.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dy}{dt}=3t^{2}-6t$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t-2$
A horizontal tangent needs $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=0$ with $\dfrac{dx}{dt}\neq 0$.
$3t(t-2)=0$
$t=0$ or $t=2$
Since $t>0$, take $t=2$, where $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2(2)-2=2\neq 0$.
$x=2^{2}-2(2)=4-4=0$
$y=2^{3}-3(2)^{2}=8-12=-4$
The tangent is horizontal at $(0,-4)$.
